item.title: Bayer Earnings Beat Estimates on Crop Science Strength
item.description: Bayer AG posted better-than-expected profit in the second quarter, helped by a strong performance in its crop science business.

item.title: Lufthansa Warns of Profit Risk as Jet Fuel Surge Roils Industry
item.description: Deutsche Lufthansa AG warned of heightened uncertainty for its full-year outlook as volatility in jet fuel prices and shortened booking cycles complicate efforts to boost profit.

item.title: Chinese Dip-Buying Bolsters Gold as Prices Find Floor at $4,000
item.description: Chinese institutional investors have swooped on gold in recent weeks, helping to arrest the precious metal’s decline and keep prices above the key threshold of $4,000 an ounce.

item.title: China’s AI Blitz Creates ‘Death Zone’ for Rival US Model Makers
item.description: A flurry of model launches from China’s AI sector is rapidly narrowing the gap with Silicon Valley and creating what’s been described as a death zone for anyone without frontier-pushing technology or market-breaking pricing.

item.title: Big AI Bets Divide Venture Capital, Leaving Smaller Funds Behind
item.description: Early last year, venture capital firm Felix Capital set out to raise $600 million for its next fund, touting previous investments in fitness-machine maker Peloton Interactive Inc. and food-delivery service Deliveroo. But investors want to see returns from older funds before they commit new capital, and Felix is still $150 million short of its target, according to a person with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Citi Says Japan Has Yen Defense Tools Beyond Treasury Sales
item.description: Japan has alternative tools to defend the yen without liquidating its more than $1.1 trillion US Treasury portfolio as its short-term debt holdings run low, according to Citigroup Inc.

item.title: Katayama Says US Evaluates Japan’s Economic Policies Highly
item.description: Washington evaluates Japan’s economic policies highly, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said, sidestepping a question on whether the US helped Japan strengthen the yen out of concern over Tokyo’s financial markets.

item.title: Modi Seeks Sweeping Tax Cuts for Electronics Firms, Global Funds
item.description: India will seek parliamentary approval for tax changes to spur foreign investment and local manufacturing, according to people with knowledge of the matter, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi works to refocus the administration on his economic agenda after recent student protests.

item.title: Apple Briefly Removes Telegram App For Child Abuse Content
item.description: Apple Inc. briefly removed the Telegram messaging app from its App Store after finding content on the platform that violated a ban on child sexual abuse material.

item.title: Confusion Over India NSE Closing Auction Turbocharges Nifty Rally
item.description: The new rules were meant to improve price discovery and curb manipulation in the final stretch of trading.

item.title: South Korea’s Leveraged ETF Trading Plummets Under New Curbs
item.description: Trading in leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to South Korea’s two chip giants has shrunk sharply, after authorities took steps to slow demand for the products that fueled recent market volatility.

item.title: Iron Ore Dips to 13-Month Low in Threat to Higher-Cost Supply
item.description: Iron ore traded near a 13-month low, pushing the market to levels that may threaten some higher-cost production.

item.title: After Historic Intervention, 155 Emerges as Yen’s Next Big Test
item.description: Japan’s historic joint intervention with the US is shifting market focus to whether the yen can strengthen beyond 155 per dollar, a threshold strategists view as the key test for the rally’s staying power.

item.title: Alibaba-Backed 3D-Modeling Startup Vast Is Said to Weigh HK IPO
item.description: Vast, a 3D-modeling startup, is considering an initial public offering in Hong Kong, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Australia Household Spending Jumps as Fuel Spike Drives EV Surge
item.description: Australia’s household spending surged beyond estimates in June as consumers accelerated a shift to electric vehicles in response to persistently elevated fuel prices.

item.title: Bessent’s Yen Rescue to Boost US Pressure on Japan Trade, Rates
item.description: The first US-Japan coordinated purchases of yen in decades was “a signal of friendship,” according to President Donald Trump. “The Trump administration delivers for America’s trusted partners,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.

item.title: Race for Diaspora Dollars Pumps Up India’s Bond, Loan Markets
item.description: A surge in dollar demand from Indian lenders racing to boost the leverage on foreign currency deposits they are offering to overseas citizens is firing up its dollar bond and loan markets, with global banks rushing to capture the business, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: NAB Tests AI Agents in Plan to Deploy Tech to Banking Customers
item.description: National Australia Bank Ltd.’s technology chief said the firm will soon begin testing the security and operational guardrails of an agentic artificial intelligence platform as the country’s largest lenders seek to deploy the technology more widely.

item.title: India RBI Seen Holding Rates as Inflation Risks Stay in Focus
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to keep interest rates unchanged on Wednesday as policymakers assess whether higher energy costs from the renewed Middle East conflict spill over into broader inflation before raising borrowing costs.

item.title: Clorox Expects Full-Year Sales Boost From Purell Deal
item.description: The Clorox Company reported earnings for its fiscal fourth quarter on Monday that beat analyst expectations, despite lower sales volumes and additional costs due to logistics and its recent acquisition of Purell hand sanitizer-maker GOJO Industries.

item.title: Gold Holds Steady With US-Iran Standoff and Fed Outlook in Focus
item.description: Gold moved in a narrow range, as traders monitored diplomatic efforts to cool US-Iran tensions, potentially pushing energy prices lower and easing pressure on the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

item.title: Korea Inflation Drops Below Estimates But Pressure Persists
item.description: South Korea’s consumer inflation slowed more than expected, falling back below 3% and after accelerating to its fastest pace since late 2023 a month earlier, easing pressure on policymakers to tighten policy.

item.title: HSBC’s Record-Breaking Stock Rally Faces Test From Earnings
item.description: A surge in HSBC Holdings Plc.’s shares to a record has raised the bar for the Asia-focused lender to deliver results that can help sustain the rally, with investors focused on capital returns, buyback prospects and the outlook.

item.title: Prabowo Eyes Bank Indonesia Chief Aligned With His Goals
item.description: Granted independence after the 1997 Asian financial crisis, Indonesia’s central bank remained one of the few institutions to retain autonomy since Prabowo Subianto became president two years ago. Now it looks set to fall more directly under his sway.

item.title: Grab Boosts Forecasts on Robust Ride, Delivery Demand
item.description: Grab Holdings Ltd. raised its annual earnings and sales forecasts, a sign that robust demand from Southeast Asian commuters is helping to absorb impact of higher fuel prices stemming from the Middle East conflict.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set for Muted Open, Oil Holds Losses: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were set for a muted open Tuesday as investors weighed a rebound in US equities against lingering uncertainty over the Middle East and whether the artificial intelligence-fueled rally has further to run. Oil held Monday’s losses.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 4
item.description: Oil was steady after its biggest drop in a week, as President Donald Trump said his latest offer of talks is Tehran’s “last chance” and that he expects a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Bessent Seeks Fed Help in Defending Yen in Unusual Call
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s call for the Federal Reserve to boost a facility that Japan can use to support its currency has put renewed attention on the ties between the two institutions, which typically operate at arm’s length.

item.title: Korean Firms Expanded Short-Term Debt Funding Before Market Rout
item.description: South Korean financial companies and other firms borrowed more money in short-term debt markets in the first half of the year amid an unprecedented stock market rally that gave way to a meltdown in recent weeks.

item.title: TMX Australia to Prioritize Tech Transition From Cboe, CEO Says
item.description: TMX Group Ltd.’s top priority after completing its purchase of Cboe Global Markets Inc.’s Australian business will be migrating clients to its own market technology, according to a senior executive.
